```{r}
theme_md_classic <- function() {
    theme_classic(
        base_size = 6, 
        base_family = "ArialMT",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6),  # was size 8 in other notebooks?
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}

theme_md_bw <- function() {
    theme_bw(
        base_size = 6, 
        base_family = "ArialMT",
        base_line_size = 0.25,
        base_rect_size = 0.25
    ) %+replace% theme(
        axis.text = element_text(color = "black", size = 6),
        axis.ticks = element_line(color = "black"),
        strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 6),
        strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 8),
        legend.text = element_text(size = 6),
        panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_rect(fill = NA, color = "black"),
        complete = TRUE
    )
}
```

## Utilities

```{r}
# just takes 2 vectors; positive is the class for which to calculate F1 score
f1_score <- function(pred, truth, positive = 1) {
    # Basic checks
    if (length(pred) != length(truth)) {
        stop("pred and truth must have the same length.")
    }
    
    # Coerce to same type
    pred  <- as.vector(pred)
    truth <- as.vector(truth)
    
    # Remove NA pairs
    keep  <- !is.na(pred) & !is.na(truth)
    pred  <- pred[keep]
    truth <- truth[keep]
    
    # Confusion components
    tp <- sum(pred == positive & truth == positive)
    fp <- sum(pred == positive & truth != positive)
    fn <- sum(pred != positive & truth == positive)
    
    # Handle edge cases
    if (tp == 0) 
        return(0)
    
    precision <- tp / (tp + fp)
    recall    <- tp / (tp + fn)
    
    if ((precision + recall) == 0) 
        return(0)
    
    2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
}


f1_per_class <- function(pred, truth) {
    if (length(pred) != length(truth)) 
        stop("pred and truth must have same length.")
    
    keep  <- !is.na(pred) & !is.na(truth)
    pred  <- pred[keep]
    truth <- truth[keep]
    
    # check all pred in truth
    unknown <- setdiff(unique(pred), unique(truth))
    if (length(unknown) > 0)
        stop("pred contains labels not present in truth: ", paste(unknown, collapse = ", "))
    
    # Ensure pred has same set of levels as truth so missing predicted classes get 0 columns
    truth_fac <- factor(truth)
    pred_fac  <- factor(pred, levels = levels(truth_fac))
    
    cm <- table(truth_fac, pred_fac)  # rows=true, cols=pred
    
    tp <- diag(cm)
    pred_pos <- colSums(cm)
    true_pos <- rowSums(cm)
    
    fp <- pred_pos - tp
    fn <- true_pos - tp
    
    precision <- ifelse(tp + fp > 0, tp / (tp + fp), 0)
    recall    <- ifelse(tp + fn > 0, tp / (tp + fn), 0)
    
    f1 <- ifelse(precision + recall > 0, 2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall), 0)
    names(f1) <- levels(truth_fac)
    return(f1)
}
```

## (Quick conclusions)

HVG > Clust_NSF > TFs > Panel > Mouse Panel > Group_NSF > ABC Tax Genes

[fraction clusters match, using all, inc. inconclusive_mapping]
marmoset_MSCA_rnaseq_HVG       0.730
marmoset_MSCA_Cluster_NSForest 0.725
marmoset_AnimalTFDB_TF         0.639
marmoset_MSCA_Xenium           0.601
mouse_ABC_Atlas_MERFISH        0.597
marmoset_MSCA_Group_NSForest   0.563
mouse_ABC_Atlas_taxonomy       0.365


Also the "inconclusive_mapping" clusters don't map any worse with the spatial
panel genes, which I think implies that the spatial panel isn't the reason that
those clusters didn't map well. 

But even if it's not the panel per se, it could still be a modality difference 
+ the panel that makes them map worse; or they could just be types that actually
are very similar across multiple structures.

Also the HVGs doing best might be circular because it was used to generate the
clusters in the first place.

```{r}
selfmmc_f1_clust %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    tibble::rownames_to_column("cluster") %>% 
    reshape2::melt(id.vars="cluster", variable.name="gene_set", value.name="F1") %>% 
    mutate(
        gene_set = sapply(
            gene_set,
```

# (!) Performance Tables for Spatial Panel

## Helper fxn

```{r}
# tbl is a raw tabulation object (2 dims, rows are predictions, columns are truths),
# e.g.: tbl <- table(df[, c("prediction", "truth")])
#
# I had chatgpt write this tedious thing but it all checks out
pred_score_fxn <- function(tbl, top_n = 3, zero_alt_as_na = TRUE) {
    # make tbl into a normal matrix
    cm <- as.matrix(unclass(tbl))
    
    storage.mode(cm) <- "numeric"
    
    if (is.null(rownames(cm)) || is.null(colnames(cm))) {
        stop("cm must have rownames (pred labels) and colnames (truth labels).")
    }
    
    pred_labels  <- rownames(cm)
    truth_labels <- colnames(cm)
    n_pred  <- rowSums(cm)
    n_truth <- colSums(cm)
    
    # Match each predicted label to the corresponding truth column (for diagonal-by-name)
    truth_col_idx <- match(pred_labels, truth_labels)
    
    # True positives per predicted class (0 if no matching truth column exists)
    tp <- numeric(length(pred_labels))
    has_match <- !is.na(truth_col_idx)
    tp[has_match] <- cm[cbind(which(has_match), truth_col_idx[has_match])]
    
    # Precision = P(truth = pred | pred)  (this is your "odds it's correct" as a probability)
    precision <- ifelse(n_pred > 0, tp / n_pred, NA_real_)
    
    # Recall for completeness (used for F1)
    recall <- rep(NA_real_, length(pred_labels))
    recall[has_match] <- ifelse(
        n_truth[truth_col_idx[has_match]] > 0,
        tp[has_match] / n_truth[truth_col_idx[has_match]],
        NA_real_
    )
    
    # F1
    f1 <- ifelse(
        is.na(precision) | is.na(recall) | (precision + recall == 0),
        0,
        2 * precision * recall / (precision + recall)
    )
    
    # Row-normalized confusion: P(truth | pred)
    denom <- pmax(n_pred, 1)  # avoid divide-by-zero
    post <- sweep(cm, 1, denom, "/", check.margin = FALSE)
    
    # Build top confusion columns
    out <- data.frame(
        prediction = pred_labels,
        n_pred     = as.integer(n_pred),
        n_truth    = as.integer(n_truth),
        precision  = precision,
        recall     = recall,
        f1         = f1,
        p_alt      = 1 - precision,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    
    # Initialize top confusion columns
    for (k in seq_len(top_n)) {
        out[[paste0("alt", k)]] <- NA_character_
        out[[paste0("p_alt", k)]] <- NA_real_
    }
    
    # Fill in top alternatives per predicted class
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(cm))) {
        pvec <- post[i, ]
        
        # Remove the "correct" class from alternatives (by matched column name)
        j <- truth_col_idx[i]
        if (!is.na(j)) pvec[j] <- 0
        
        ord <- order(pvec, decreasing = TRUE)
        
        if (zero_alt_as_na) {
            ord <- ord[pvec[ord] > 0]
        }
        
        if (length(ord) == 0) next
        
        take <- head(ord, top_n)
        for (k in seq_along(take)) {
            out[[paste0("alt", k)]][i]   <- truth_labels[take[k]]
            out[[paste0("p_alt", k)]][i] <- pvec[take[k]]
        }
    }
    rownames(out) <- NULL
    
    # rounding for pretty
    for (cname in colnames(out)) {
        if (is.numeric(out[[cname]])) {
            out[[cname]] <- round(out[[cname]], 4)
        }
    }
    out
}
```


## Cluster

another cluster? And what is that cluster?"

believed, and if anything is interchangeable.

```{r}
        pred  = factor(pred,  levels = rownames(obs)),
```

# More Analysis (using output tables)

## (Which class is the worst based on group-level accuracy?)

```{r}
pred_accuracy_table_group %>% 
    (function(x) {
        df <- unique(obs[, c("Subcortex_Group_v4", "Subcortex_Class_v4")])
        nm_map <- setNames(df$Subcortex_Class_v4, df$Subcortex_Group_v4)
        x$class <- nm_map[x$prediction]
        x
    }) %>% 
    split(., .$class) %>% 
    sapply(. %>% .[, 2:4] %>% sapply(mean)) %>% 
    t %>% 
    as.data.frame %>% 
    .[order(.$f1), ] %>% 
    print.data.frame
```

## Plots

### Cluster-level

```{r}
pred_accuracy_table %>% 
    .[, c("prediction", "precision", "recall", "f1")] %>% 
    reshape2::melt(id.vars="prediction", variable.name="metric", value.name="score") %>% 
    mutate(metric=factor(metric, levels=rev(c("precision", "recall", "f1")))) %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(score, metric)
    ) + 
    geom_boxplot(linewidth=0.25, outlier.shape=16, outlier.size=0.5) + 
    # labs(title = "Multiome RNA Self-Mapping\nPerformance at the Cluster-Level", y=NULL, x=NULL) +
    labs(title = "Multiome RNA Self-Mapping\nPerformance at the Cluster-Level") +
    scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) + 
    theme_md_classic() -> p1
p1
```


```{r}
pred_accuracy_table %>% 
    .[, c("prediction", "precision", "recall", "f1")] %>% 
    reshape2::melt(id.vars="prediction", variable.name="metric", value.name="score") %>% 
    mutate(metric=factor(metric, levels=rev(c("precision", "recall", "f1")))) %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(metric, score)
    ) + 
    geom_boxplot(linewidth=0.25, outlier.shape=16, outlier.size=0.5) + 
    labs(title = "Cluster-Level") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), expand=c(0,0)) + 
    theme_md_classic() + 
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle=30, hjust=1, vjust=1)) -> p3
p3
```

MMC is better at retaining true calls than keeping pure. that could explain
why the metacells look pretty good: individual assignments might be a little
messy but on the whole the cluster has a lot of true positives.

also outliers: clusters for which, if the classifer calls it, it's like always
wrong.

# Identify confusion hot spots

Ideas:
Low `precision` + High `n_pred` = impure prediction labels
Large `n_pred` * `p_alt1` = big confusion flow

(in hindsight, de-emphasized n_pred in final outputs; not as concerned with
support as just performance for all cell types in taxonomy)

## Group-level weighted precision

```{r}
# weighted by number of cells in each Group
pred_accuracy_table_group %>% 
    (function(x) {
        weights <- x$n_truth / sum(x$n_truth)
        sum(x$precision * weights)
    }) 
# [1] 0.9145346

# weighted by number of cells in each prediction Group
pred_accuracy_table_group %>% 
    (function(x) {
        weights <- x$n_pred/ sum(x$n_pred)
        sum(x$precision * weights)
    }) 
# [1] 0.9019268

## the unweighted (fraction of cells with correct group label)
sum(diag(tbl_group)) / sum(tbl_group)
# [1] 0.9019291
```

Similar no matter how you cut it

### (skip) Alluvial plot

“left = truth, right = prediction” alluvial where each truth group has total width = 1,

```{r}
library(tidyr)
library(ggalluvial)

make_truth_alluvial_df <- function(
        tbl_group,
        pred_accuracy_table_group,
        n_worst = 25,
        recall_max = NULL,
        p_min = 0.05,
        top_k = NULL,
        include_self = TRUE,
        other_label = "Other"
) {
    cm <- as.matrix(unclass(tbl_group))
    storage.mode(cm) <- "numeric"
    
    # Column-normalize: P(pred | truth)
    p_pred_given_truth <- sweep(cm, 2, pmax(colSums(cm), 1), "/")
    
    # truth-centered performance table
    truth_scores <- pred_accuracy_table_group %>%
        transmute(truth = prediction, recall = recall, n_truth = n_truth) %>%
        filter(truth %in% colnames(p_pred_given_truth)) %>%
        filter(!is.na(recall), n_truth > 0)
    
    truth_keep <- if (!is.null(recall_max)) {
        truth_scores %>% filter(recall <= recall_max) %>% arrange(recall) %>% pull(truth)
    } else {
        truth_scores %>% arrange(recall) %>% slice_head(n = n_worst) %>% pull(truth)
    }
    
    # Long format probs for selected truth groups
    df <- as.data.frame(as.table(p_pred_given_truth[, truth_keep, drop = FALSE]), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(df) <- c("pred", "truth", "p")
    
    # add class annotation (for fill, etc.)
    df <- df %>%
        left_join(
            pred_accuracy_table_group %>% select(prediction, Subcortex_Class_v4),
            by = c("truth" = "prediction")
        )
    
    df2 <- df %>%
        group_by(truth) %>%
        mutate(
            is_self = (pred == truth),
            rank_p = dplyr::min_rank(dplyr::desc(p)),
            topk_keep = if (is.null(top_k)) FALSE else (rank_p <= top_k),
            keep =
                (include_self & is_self) |
                (!is_self & (p >= p_min)) |
                (!is_self & topk_keep),
            pred2 = ifelse(keep, pred, other_label)
        ) %>%
        group_by(truth, pred2, Subcortex_Class_v4) %>%
        summarise(p = sum(p), .groups = "drop")
    
    # Order truth groups by recall (worst first)
    truth_order <- truth_scores %>%
        filter(truth %in% truth_keep) %>%
        arrange(recall) %>%
        pull(truth)
    
    df2 %>%
        mutate(
            truth = factor(truth, levels = truth_order),
            pred2 = factor(pred2, levels = c(setdiff(unique(pred2), other_label), other_label))
        )
}
```

### Build edges

```{r}
confusion_edges <- function(tbl) {
    cm <- as.matrix(unclass(tbl))
    storage.mode(cm) <- "numeric"
    
    pred_labels  <- rownames(cm)
    truth_labels <- colnames(cm)
    n_pred <- rowSums(cm)
    
    # long format
    edges <- as.data.frame(as.table(cm), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(edges) <- c("pred", "truth", "n")
    
    # add row-normalized probability P(truth | pred)
    edges <- edges %>%
        mutate(
            n_pred = n_pred[match(pred, pred_labels)],
            p_pred_to_truth = ifelse(n_pred > 0, n / n_pred, NA_real_)
        ) %>%
        filter(pred != truth, n > 0)
    
    edges
}
```

```{r}
tbl_group %>% 
    confusion_edges %>% 
    filter(n >= 50, p_pred_to_truth >= 0.05) %>%  # tune thresholds
    arrange(desc(n)) ->
    edges_group
```

### (Plot flows)

```{r}
library(grid)
library(tibble)

plot_confusion_arrows <- function(edges, metrics_tbl, top_n = 20) {
    ed <- edges %>%
        # arrange(desc(n)) %>%
        arrange(desc(p_pred_to_truth)) %>% 
        slice_head(n = top_n)
    
    labels_used <- union(ed$pred, ed$truth)
    
    node_order <- metrics_tbl %>%
        filter(prediction %in% labels_used) %>%
        mutate(conf_burden = n_pred * (1 - precision)) %>%
        arrange(desc(conf_burden)) %>%
        pull(prediction) %>%
        unique()
    
    # Pre-name columns to avoid x/y collisions
    nodes_left <- tibble(
        pred = node_order,
        x = 0,
        y = rev(seq_along(node_order))
    ) %>% 
        left_join(
            metrics_tbl %>% select(prediction, Subcortex_Class_v4),
            by = c("pred" = "prediction")
        )
    
    nodes_right <- tibble(
        truth = node_order,
        xend = 1,
        yend = rev(seq_along(node_order))
    ) %>% 
        left_join(
            metrics_tbl %>% select(prediction, Subcortex_Class_v4),
            by = c("truth" = "prediction")
        )
    
    ed2 <- ed %>%
        left_join(nodes_left, by = "pred") %>%
        left_join(nodes_right, by = "truth") %>%
        left_join(
            metrics_tbl %>% select(prediction, Subcortex_Class_v4),
            by = c("pred" = "prediction")
        )
    
    ggplot() +
        geom_curve(
            data = ed2,
            aes(
                x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend,
                # linewidth = n, 
                linewidth = p_pred_to_truth, 
                # alpha = p_pred_to_truth, 
                alpha = n, 
                color = Subcortex_Class_v4
            ),
            curvature = 0.15,
            arrow = arrow(length = unit(2.2, "mm"), type = "closed")
        ) +
        geom_point(data = nodes_left, aes(x, y, color=Subcortex_Class_v4), size = 2) +
        geom_point(data = nodes_right, aes(xend, yend, color=Subcortex_Class_v4), size = 2) +
        geom_text(data = nodes_left, aes(x, y, label = pred), hjust = 1.05, size = 3) +
        geom_text(data = nodes_right, aes(xend, yend, label = truth), hjust = -0.05, size = 3) +
        scale_x_continuous(
            breaks = c(0, 1),
            labels = c("Predicted", "True"),
            expand = c(0.15, 0.15)
        ) +
        # scale_size_continuous(name = "Confused cells") +
        scale_size_continuous(name = "P(truth | pred)") +
        # scale_alpha_continuous(name = "P(truth | pred)") +
        scale_alpha_continuous(name = "Confused cells") +
        scale_color_manual(values = palettes$Class) +
        coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
        theme_md_classic() +
        theme(
            legend.position = "right",
            plot.margin = margin(10, 120, 10, 120),
            axis.line = element_blank(),
            axis.text.y = element_blank(),
            axis.title = element_blank(),
            axis.ticks = element_blank()
        )
}
```

### (Heatmap)

```{r}
library(tidyr)

plot_hotspot_confusion_heatmap <- function(tbl, metrics_tbl, top_rows = 12, p_label_min = 0.05) {
    cm <- as.matrix(unclass(tbl))
    storage.mode(cm) <- "numeric"
    
    # Row-normalized: P(truth | pred)
    post <- sweep(cm, 1, pmax(rowSums(cm), 1), "/")
    
    # Pick hotspot predicted labels
    hot_rows <- metrics_tbl %>%
        mutate(conf_flow1 = n_pred * p_alt1) %>%
        arrange(desc(conf_flow1)) %>%
        slice_head(n = top_rows) %>%
        pull(prediction)
    
    # Include likely alternative truths
    hot_cols <- metrics_tbl %>%
        filter(prediction %in% hot_rows) %>%
        select(alt1, alt2, alt3) %>%
        unlist(use.names = FALSE) %>%
        unique() %>%
        na.omit()
    
    show_cols <- unique(c(hot_rows, hot_cols))
    show_rows <- hot_rows
    
    # Subset matrices
    post_sub <- post[show_rows, show_cols, drop = FALSE]
    cm_sub   <- cm[show_rows, show_cols, drop = FALSE]
    
    # Long format
    df_p <- as.data.frame(as.table(post_sub), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(df_p) <- c("pred", "truth", "p")
    
    df_n <- as.data.frame(as.table(cm_sub), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(df_n) <- c("pred", "truth", "n")
    
    df <- df_p %>%
        left_join(df_n, by = c("pred", "truth")) %>%
        left_join(metrics_tbl %>% select(prediction, Subcortex_Class_v4),
                  by = c("pred" = "prediction")) %>%
        mutate(
            pred = factor(pred, levels = rev(show_rows)),
            truth = factor(truth, levels = show_cols),
            label = ifelse(p >= p_label_min, sprintf("%.2f\n(n=%d)", p, n), "")
        )
    
    ggplot(df, aes(truth, pred, fill = p)) +
        geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
        geom_text(aes(label = label), size = 2.5, lineheight = 0.9) +
        scale_fill_viridis_c(name = "P(truth | pred)", limits = c(0, 1)) +
        labs(x = "True group", y = "Predicted group") +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
        theme(
            axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
            panel.grid = element_blank()
        )
}
```

#### Reciprocal confusion (normalized)

Want to normalize the confusion (so make probabilities or fractions)

```{r}
pair_confusions_from_tbl <- function(tbl) {
    cm <- as.matrix(unclass(tbl))
    storage.mode(cm) <- "numeric"
    
    pred_labels  <- rownames(cm)
    truth_labels <- colnames(cm)
    
    # supports by truth label (denominator side)
    truth_support <- colSums(cm)
    truth_df <- tibble(
        label = names(truth_support),
        n_truth = as.numeric(truth_support)
    )
    
    # long off-diagonal confusion edges
    edges <- as.data.frame(as.table(cm), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    colnames(edges) <- c("pred", "truth", "n")
    edges <- edges %>%
        filter(pred != truth, n > 0)
    
    # collapse to unordered pairs
    pairs <- edges %>%
        mutate(
            a = pmin(pred, truth),
            b = pmax(pred, truth),
            # direction-specific counts within the unordered pair
            n_a_to_b = ifelse(pred == a & truth == b, n, 0),
            n_b_to_a = ifelse(pred == b & truth == a, n, 0)
        ) %>%
        group_by(a, b) %>%
        summarise(
            n_a_to_b = sum(n_a_to_b),
            n_b_to_a = sum(n_b_to_a),
            n_pair   = n_a_to_b + n_b_to_a,
            .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        left_join(truth_df %>% rename(a = label, n_truth_a = n_truth), by = "a") %>%
        left_join(truth_df %>% rename(b = label, n_truth_b = n_truth), by = "b") %>%
        mutate(
            truth_pair = n_truth_a + n_truth_b,
            pair_swap_frac = ifelse(truth_pair > 0, n_pair / truth_pair, NA_real_),
            frac_a_to_b = ifelse(n_truth_b > 0, n_a_to_b / n_truth_b, NA_real_), # truth=B miscalled as A
            frac_b_to_a = ifelse(n_truth_a > 0, n_b_to_a / n_truth_a, NA_real_), # truth=A miscalled as B
            asymmetry = ifelse(n_pair > 0, abs(n_a_to_b - n_b_to_a) / n_pair, NA_real_)
        ) %>%
        arrange(desc(n_pair))
    
    pairs
}
```

#### (!) What fraction of group misassignments explained there?

Those (labelled) swap pairs explain what fraction of group misassignments?

```{r}
# library(dplyr)
# library(tibble)

cm <- as.matrix(unclass(tbl_group))
storage.mode(cm) <- "numeric"

# Total number of wrong assignments at group level
N_wrong_total <- sum(cm) - sum(diag(cm))   # off-diagonal sum

# 2) Recreate pairs_group (must include n_pair, truth_pair, pair_swap_frac, etc.)
# (Assumes you already have pair_confusions_from_tbl() from earlier; if not, tell me and I’ll paste it)
pairs_group <- pair_confusions_from_tbl(tbl_group)

# 3) Recreate label selection logic (exactly what you used in the plot)
must_label_pairs <- tibble::tribble(
    ~a,                  ~b,
    "Oligo OPALIN",       "Oligo PLEKHG1",
    "STRd D1 Matrix MSN", "STRv D1 MSN",
    "THM GABA",           "THM-MB GABA",
    "STRd D2 Matrix MSN", "STRd D2 Striosome MSN",
    "STRd D2 Matrix MSN", "STRv D2 MSN",
    "STRd D1 Matrix MSN", "STRd D1 Striosome MSN",
    "L2-3 IT CTX Glut",   "L4-5 IT CTX-PArCx Glut",
    "MB-THM GABA",        "THM-MB GABA",
    "CA2-CA3-IG Glut",    "CA3 Glut",
    "VLN Glut",           "VP-MG Glut",
    "STR TAC3-PLPP4 GABA", "STR-BF TAC3-PLPP4-LHX8 GABA",
    "LSX PRDM12-NTS GABA", "LSX PRDM12-SLIT2 GABA"
)

canon_pair <- function(a, b) tibble(a0 = pmin(a, b), b0 = pmax(a, b))
must_pairs_canon <- canon_pair(must_label_pairs$a, must_label_pairs$b) %>%
    mutate(must_label = TRUE)

pairs_labeled <- pairs_group %>%
    left_join(must_pairs_canon, by = c("a" = "a0", "b" = "b0")) %>%
    mutate(must_label = ifelse(is.na(must_label), FALSE, must_label)) %>%
    mutate(
        rank_swap  = dense_rank(desc(pair_swap_frac)),
        rank_npair = dense_rank(desc(n_pair))
    ) %>%
    mutate(
        label_me = must_label
    ) %>%
    filter(label_me) %>%
    select(a, b, n_pair)

# 4) Compute how many wrong assignments are in those labeled pairs
# Since a,b are canonical with a<b, the pair confusion count in the full matrix is:
# cm[a,b] + cm[b,a]
N_wrong_labeled <- sum(mapply(function(a, b) cm[a, b] + cm[b, a], pairs_labeled$a, pairs_labeled$b))

frac_explained <- N_wrong_labeled / N_wrong_total

list(
    N_wrong_total   = N_wrong_total,
    N_wrong_labeled = N_wrong_labeled,
    frac_explained  = frac_explained,
    n_labeled_pairs = nrow(pairs_labeled)
)

# $N_wrong_total
# [1] 66582
# 
# $N_wrong_labeled
# [1] 31551
# 
# $frac_explained
# [1] 0.4738668
# 
# $n_labeled_pairs
# [1] 12
```

So those labelled swaps explain ~47% of mis-assigned groups in self-mapping.

# Cluster donor composition vs self-mapping

Does donor composition affect self-mapping performance?

For each cluster, calculate Shannon entropy, and normalize to: 
0 for single-donor cluster
1 for perfectly even 4 donor mixing

(the raw shannon entropy will max at log(4)).

```{r}
donor_entropy <- donor_counts %>%
    group_by(Cluster_v4) %>%
    summarize(
        total_cells = sum(n_cell),
        n_donors_observed = sum(n_cell > 0),
        entropy = {
            p <- n_cell / sum(n_cell)
            -sum(p[p > 0] * log(p[p > 0]))
        },
        entropy_norm = entropy / log(4),
        # also normalize by number of donors (so if 2 donors, 1 if 50/50)
        entropy_obs_norm = ifelse(
            n_donors_observed > 1,
            entropy / log(n_donors_observed),
            0
        ),
        max_donor_frac = max(n_cell / sum(n_cell)),
        .groups = "drop"
    )

donor_entropy
```

```{r}
donor_entropy %>% 
    ggplot(aes(rank(entropy_norm), entropy_norm)) + 
    geom_line() + 
    theme_md_classic()

# only maxes at 1 if 4 donors
pred_accuracy_table %>% 
    left_join(donor_entropy, by = join_by("prediction" == "Cluster_v4")) %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(entropy_norm, f1)
    ) + 
    geom_point() + 
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    ggpubr::stat_regline_equation(label.y=0.1) + 
    ggpubr::stat_cor(label.y=0.05) + 
    labs(
        x = "Donor Entropy for Cluster",
        y = "Cluster F1 Score",
        title = "Self-Mapping Performance vs. Donor Representation"
    ) + 
    theme_md_classic()

# entropy scaled by number of donors (so if 2 donors, entropy 1 if 50/50)
pred_accuracy_table %>% 
    left_join(donor_entropy, by = join_by("prediction" == "Cluster_v4")) %>% 
    ggplot(
        aes(entropy_obs_norm, f1)
    ) + 
    geom_point() + 
    geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
    ggpubr::stat_regline_equation(label.y=0.1) + 
    ggpubr::stat_cor(label.y=0.05) + 
    labs(
        x = "Donor Entropy for Cluster",
        y = "Cluster F1 Score",
        title = "Self-Mapping Performance vs. Donor Representation"
    ) + 
    theme_md_classic()
```
